newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close lower on late selling.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close lower on late selling.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed lower on Friday as late selling swept the market amid the absence of encouraging news to lift it out of a doldrum, brokers said.
The weighted index closed 47.72 points or 0.72 percent down at an intra-session low of 6,581.96.
Turnover was a modest T$43.46 billion.

Losses were spread across the board, with export-oriented textiles and electronics showing most resilience against profit-taking. Electronics, fuelled recently by sound earning reports, fell 0.27 percent while textiles, seen to enjoy strong exports in the fourth quarter, dropped 0.25 percent.
"Investors began taking profits early and the selling kept building after the index showed no signs of recovering," said Lin Long-hsien, analyst for United Securities.

The market, prior to losses on Thursday and Friday, had gained nearly 300 points in one week after the government freed one major state fund to invest in stocks and relaxed the investment cap for another.

The heavily weighted financial sector, a chief beneficiary of the liberalisation measures, suffered strong profit-taking to fall 0.92 percent. First Commercial, one of the "Big Three" state-run banks, eased T$2 or 1.2 percent to T$165.
The other two of the Big Three banks, Chang Hwa and Hua Nan, both lost T$1, or 0.6 percent and 0.8 percent, to close at T$154 and T$124 respectively.
Brokers expected the overall market to slide into a conoslidation phase in the near term.
A 6,550-6,610 range was seen for Saturday.
